transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, well, honestly, what finally made me come in is that I keep getting up during these really long sales strategy meetings at work. Like, I know I’m supposed to stay seated, but I just can't, so I'll get up to refill my water or go pace by the printer. Which reminds me, our printer has been jamming constantly lately, like every time I try to print out the quarterly projections, it just eats the paper. My coworker, Dave—he's the one who sits next to the breakroom—he tried to fix it last week and ended up getting toner all over his favorite shirt. It was this really nice light blue button-down, too. I felt so bad for him, but I told him club soda works wonders on stains. Anyway, yeah, I just keep leaving my seat when I shouldn't be.
Have you had times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

No, not really. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get at least seven or eight hours, I'm practically a zombie the next day. Actually, I just bought one of those memory foam mattresses that comes vacuum-sealed in a box because my old one was dipping so badly in the middle. Getting it up the stairs to my apartment was a total nightmare, though. It was incredibly heavy. I had to ask my neighbor, Mark, for help, and he has this really adorable golden retriever that always tries to carry its own leash in its mouth when they go for walks. It's the cutest thing. We ended up standing in the hallway talking for like twenty minutes about dog training, which is kind of funny because I don't even own a dog, I just watch a lot of those animal rescue videos on TikTok before bed. But um... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, sleeping less. Yeah, no, I never feel energized if I skip sleep.
Before age 12, did you already have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, oh, definitely. I remember this starting way before high school. Like, my elementary school teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but I rushed through everything, talked out of turn, and forgot my homework. My desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers. Actually, I found one of those old report cards when I was helping my mom clean out her attic last Thanksgiving. We spent the whole weekend going through these dusty boxes, and she kept trying to get me to take this huge collection of vintage Pyrex bowls she has. They're that really pretty turquoise color, which I guess is super trendy right now, but I have absolutely no space in my kitchen for them. My apartment's kitchen is basically a closet. I barely have room for my coffee maker, and I cannot function without coffee. I actually just ordered this new local roast online that's supposed to have notes of blueberry and dark chocolate, which sounds amazing, right? But anyway, yeah, the sitting still thing... it's been an issue since I was little.
Do you often feel driven to keep moving, like you’re “on the go” even when you’re trying to relax?

Yeah, I mean, I guess so? It's hard to explain, but I don't really know how to just... do nothing. Like, even if I'm trying to watch a movie on the couch, I'm usually shaking my leg or I have to be doing something with my hands. I actually took up knitting for a little bit because I thought it would help me relax while I watch TV. I went to this really cute little yarn shop downtown, you know the one near that amazing bakery with the sourdough croissants? Oh my gosh, their croissants are incredible. I usually go there on Saturday mornings, but the line has been getting so long lately. I think they got featured on some food blog or something. It's great for their business, obviously, but it makes it so hard to just grab a quick coffee and pastry. I tried making my own sourdough starter once during the pandemic, like everyone else did, but I completely forgot to feed it and it turned this weird gray color and smelled like old gym socks. I had to throw the whole jar away, which was a bummer because it was one of my favorite mason jars. But um, what were we talking about? Oh, being on the go. Yeah, I just... I don't really know if I feel "driven" to keep moving, I just always kind of am moving, I guess. I don't really sit still well.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to pay attention?

Oh, completely. It's actually a huge problem at work. Like, we have these really long strategy meetings, or I'll be sitting down to read a new client brief. I just got this one brief last week for a company that makes those eco-friendly bamboo toothbrushes? Which, by the way, I tried switching to a few months ago because I'm really trying to reduce my plastic waste. I watched this
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about things unless there's an actual reason to. Like, if a deadline is coming up, sure, but I don't just worry out of nowhere. I actually have a friend, Sarah, who worries about literally everything. We were supposed to go on a road trip last summer to see this indie band play at a festival in the desert. It was going to be so fun, we rented this vintage VW camper van—which, let me tell you, looks amazing on Instagram but drives like a lawnmower. The clutch was so stiff my leg was sore for three days. Anyway, Sarah spent the whole drive panicking that we were going to run out of gas, even though I had the GPS pulled up and mapped out all the gas stations. She even brought this huge emergency kit with flares and a thermal blanket. I was like, Sarah, we're driving through California, not the Arctic tundra! We did end up getting a flat tire, though, right outside of Joshua Tree. Have you ever been to Joshua Tree? The stars out there are just unbelievable. You can see the Milky Way so clearly. I tried to take a picture with my phone, but it just looked like a black square with a couple of white dots. I really need to get a proper DSLR camera if I'm going to keep going on these trips.
